summary: The new singleton-trace explanation has the correct intended argument, but its subject is imprecise: the original members with disjoint residues, rather than the residues themselves, form the forbidden sunflower with R. One short referent correction is needed so the prose explicitly invokes sunflower-freeness of the four-uniform family.
required_revisions: In Section 4’s repaired singleton-trace paragraph, replace “disjoint residues together with R would form a sunflower” with “two original members whose residues are disjoint, together with R, would form a sunflower with core equal to their common trace point” (or an equivalent explicit statement).

findings.statement: The phrase “disjoint residues together with R would form a sunflower” names two triples and a four-set. Those residues are not themselves members of the four-uniform family H, so that literal statement does not invoke the relevant sunflower-free hypothesis. Reattaching the common trace point gives the intended three original members and common singleton core.
findings.disposition: Name the original members and their singleton core explicitly. This is a local exposition repair, not a counterexample to the intended trace bound.

checks.scope: Skeptical antecedent and referent audit of the repaired Section 4 argument
checks.method: Read the exact new paragraph and instantiated an anchor R, common point v and two disjoint three-element residues outside R; computed intersections after restoring v.
checks.observation: For S=T∪{v} and S′=T′∪{v}, exact trace gives S∩R=S′∩R={v}, and disjoint residues give S∩S′={v}. Thus S,S′,R are the forbidden members. T,T′,R also have empty pairwise intersections but T and T′ are not four-element members of H, so that reading is insufficient. The explicit repair preserves the intended inference that the residue family is intersecting.
